resources.string: A private journal, kept on your phone
Your journal is encrypted on this device and unlocks with your fingerprint, face or screen lock.
Set up a screen lock on this device first. Terpoir uses it to protect your journal.
The device\'s secure key storage did not respond. Try again.
This journal was saved by a newer version of Terpoir. Update the app to open it. Nothing was changed.
The journal couldn\'t be opened. Nothing was changed; try again.
Your fingerprints or face changed, so this device\'s key no longer works. Unlock with your recovery key.
What were you doing when this happened? (optional)

This report holds nothing from your journal. You can edit or delete anything in it before sending. If it shows a bug, what you wrote and the details above may be posted as a public issue on GitHub, without your name or email address.
No email app found. You can write to %1$s.
Terpoir closed unexpectedly last time. Send a report so it can be fixed? It says only where in the app it happened, nothing from your journal, and opens in your email app so you can check it first.
Terpoir is a self-tracking journal, not a medical device: it doesn\'t diagnose, treat, cure or prevent any condition. For medical advice, diagnosis or treatment, talk to a healthcare professional.

Looks for patterns in your own ratings, such as which terpenes or methods you tend to rate higher, and shows the sessions behind each one. Plain averages, computed on this phone when you open Insights.

Nothing leaves your phone. Insights are worked out from your encrypted journal each time and never stored. What you dismiss or hide is remembered in your encrypted journal, so it syncs to your other devices and comes back with an export.
No one else. Insights describe your own sessions; they are never advice.
Turn it off here. Insights disappear, and what you dismissed or hid is forgotten on every device you sync with.
Lets you mark Re-up Spots where you want a reminder. When you leave one after a stop of a few minutes, Terpoir asks \"Quick log?\" and opens receipt scan. At most once a day per spot.

Android\'s location service watches those spots, so it holds their coordinates, as with \"Notify me\". It needs location \"all the time\". The reminder never names the spot, and no record of your visits is kept: only that you are inside one of the spots, until you leave.
Android\'s location service (and on Google Play builds, Google Play services) knows the watched areas. Anyone who sees your notifications sees only \"Quick log?\".
Turn it off here. The watched areas are removed at once, and any pending reminder is cleared.

Keeps your journal in step across your devices through a folder you choose: a Syncthing folder, or Google Drive, Nextcloud or Dropbox through their apps. Terpoir writes encrypted sync files there and reads the ones your other devices wrote. It syncs while Terpoir is open.

Only encrypted files. The sync files open only with your journal\'s keys; they are padded and randomly named, so their contents, size and number of entries stay hidden. One more file, terpoir.key, holds your journal\'s key locked by your recovery key, so a new phone can restore from the folder with that recovery key. Terpoir itself still has no internet access for this.

Whatever syncs that folder (your cloud drive provider, or your own devices with Syncthing) stores the encrypted files and can see when you sync and roughly how much data there is. No one can read them without your keys.
Turn it off here. Terpoir stops syncing and gives up access to the folder. Files already written stay there, encrypted; delete them in your files app if you want.
Choose the folder to sync through. Use the same folder on each device.
The last sync didn\'t work. Tap Sync to try again.
Couldn\'t sync: the folder didn\'t take the files. Check that it\'s still there and you can write to it, or choose a folder in your phone\'s storage that Syncthing or your cloud app syncs.
That folder\'s app doesn\'t let Terpoir keep access to it. Choose a folder in your phone\'s storage instead, one that Syncthing or your cloud app syncs.
Some synced changes were made by a newer version of Terpoir. Update the app to bring them in.

plurals.item: Brought in %1$d file from your other devices.

resources.string: Adds a section to each session for symptoms you were hoping to ease, such as sleep or pain, and whether the session helped. This is self-tracking, never medical advice.
Nothing leaves your phone. Symptoms are stored only in your encrypted journal.
No one else. Symptoms are health information, so the section stays hidden until you turn it on.
Turn it off here. Terpoir asks whether to keep what you recorded, hidden, or delete it.
Keep the symptoms you\'ve recorded, hidden until you turn this on again, or delete them from every session?
Blocks screenshots, screen recording and casting of Terpoir, and hides it in your recent apps. Screen readers and other accessibility tools keep working.
When off, screenshots and recordings of Terpoir are saved to your photo gallery, and from there to any cloud backup it syncs with.
When off, anyone you cast or share your screen with sees your journal, and so does any app allowed to capture your screen.
Lets you open the lab-results (COA) link from a label\'s QR code in your browser. Scanned links are saved with the product either way.
When on, opening a link sends a request to the lab\'s or brand\'s website.
That website and its host learn your IP address, when you looked, and which batch you bought, since the link usually names it. Your network provider can see which site you visited.
Alerts you when you\'ve stopped at one of your saved spots, even when Terpoir is closed. Only spots with a location are watched.

Nothing leaves the phone. To watch for your spots, Android\'s location service holds their coordinates (never their names), and Terpoir needs precise location \"all the time\" and permission to notify you.

Android\'s location service knows where your spots are and when you\'re near one, and so does Google Play services on phones that use it. Alerts say only \"Did you hit a spot?\" unless you turn on names or details below.
Turn it off here. Terpoir removes every spot from Android\'s location service and clears any alert still showing. You can also take back the location permission in Android\'s settings.
When you log a session, Terpoir can remind you later to note how it went: about 90 minutes after an edible or drink, 45 after a tincture. You choose per session, and can change the time.
Nothing leaves the phone. The reminder waits in Android\'s scheduler, which knows when it will go off but nothing about the session.
The reminder says only \"Quick check-in?\", at every alert setting. Anyone who sees your screen sees that, and when.
Turn it off here. Terpoir cancels the waiting reminder and clears it if it\'s showing.
Alerts say which spot you\'re at, like \"You\'re at Spot 3\", instead of \"Did you hit a spot?\".
Nothing leaves the phone. To show a name while the journal is locked, Terpoir keeps a small list of your spots\' names outside the encrypted journal, on this phone only and never in backups.

Anyone who sees your unlocked screen, apps you\'ve allowed to read notifications, connected watches, notification history, and Android\'s notification summaries. The lock screen still shows only \"Did you hit a spot?\".
Turn it off here. The names are deleted from that list, and alerts go back to \"Did you hit a spot?\" unless details are on.
Alerts show the spot\'s name and how your sessions there went: the average rating, how many sessions, and the last product.
Nothing leaves the phone. Those details join the names in the small list kept outside the encrypted journal, on this phone only and never in backups.

The same as for names: anyone who sees your unlocked screen, notification-reading apps, connected watches, notification history and Android\'s summaries. The lock screen still shows only \"Did you hit a spot?\".
Turn it off here. The details are deleted from that list; names stay only if \"Spot names in alerts\" is on.
Reads receipts and labels with Google\'s ML Kit, through Google Play services, instead of the open engine. It\'s usually more accurate on photographed receipts, and it still runs on this phone.

Your photos and the text in them never leave the phone. Google Play services downloads and updates the recognition model, and Google\'s terms let it collect usage data, such as how often text recognition runs, never what you scanned. If your version of Terpoir has the online map, ML Kit can send that usage data from Terpoir while this is on.
Google, through Play services, learns that you use text recognition. ML Kit is closed source, so what it does can\'t be checked the way the open engine can be.
Turn it off here. Scans go back to the open engine, and Terpoir tells Play services it no longer needs the model, so Play services can remove it.
Turn it off here. Pages you already opened stay in your browser\'s history until you clear it.

Lets you pick a spot\'s location on a map instead of using your phone\'s location. The map comes over the internet from OpenFreeMap, a free map service with no account or key, or from MapTiler if you add your own MapTiler key.

While you use the map, your IP address and the areas you look at go to the map provider. Looking around a spot shows roughly where it is. Nothing from your journal is sent, and map images aren\'t kept on your phone.

The map provider sees the areas you view and your IP address: OpenFreeMap, a free service run by one person on donations, or MapTiler, a map company, if you chose it. Your internet provider can see which one you use, but not which areas.

Turn it off here. Terpoir stops all map requests, deletes anything the map stored and goes back to OpenFreeMap. Locations you already picked stay with your spots, and a saved MapTiler key stays until you remove it.
When you open your journal, Terpoir checks your location once and shows a saved spot you\'re near, so you can log a session there.
Nothing leaves your phone. The location is checked only while Terpoir is open, compared with your spots inside the encrypted journal, and not kept. Nothing is registered with Android for alerts.
Android knows Terpoir asked for your location while open, as with any app. No one else sees your spots.
Turn it off here. You can also take away the location permission in Android\'s settings.
The new-note button starts listening right away, using your phone\'s on-device speech recognition. Turn off to start with the keyboard instead.
Nothing. Your voice is turned into text on your phone, never sent to an online service, and the recording isn\'t kept. When off, notes are typed, and your keyboard app sees everything you type.
People nearby can hear what you say. With typing, your keyboard app sees your words, and third-party keyboards may send them elsewhere.
Change it here at any time. You can always switch between voice and typing in the note itself.
Turn it back on here. Screenshots already taken stay in your gallery until you delete them.
Are you of legal age to use cannabis where you live?
Google Play may tell Terpoir an age range for your account. Terpoir only checks it on this phone, to keep out under-18s, and never stores or sends it.
Come back when you\'re of legal age where you live.
Type the recovery key of the journal you exported. It opens the export on this phone; capitals and dashes don\'t matter.
That file isn\'t a Terpoir export.
This was made by a newer version of Terpoir. Update the app, then try again. Nothing was changed.
The journal couldn\'t be restored. Nothing was kept; try again.
Do you already have a Terpoir journal?
Bring your journal to this phone
Where is it? You\'ll need its recovery key.
A file you saved with \"Export\" in the Privacy Center.
The folder your other device syncs through: a Syncthing folder, or Google Drive, Nextcloud or Dropbox.

Type your journal\'s recovery key. It opens the journal in this folder; capitals and dashes don\'t matter. Terpoir then keeps syncing through this folder, which you can turn off in the Privacy Center.
That folder has no Terpoir journal key. Open Terpoir on a device that syncs through it, sync once, then try again.
None of the files in that folder open with its key. Sync once from a device that has the journal, then try again.

Export saves your whole journal as one encrypted file, and only your recovery key opens it, so keep the two apart. Use it to move to a new phone: choose \"Restore from an export\" when setting Terpoir up there. Import merges an export of this same journal back in.
Saved. Only your recovery key opens it.

This saves your whole journal as readable files (JSON and spreadsheet-friendly CSV, in one ZIP), to move it to another app or keep your own copy. Unlike everything else in Terpoir, they are not encrypted: anyone or any app that gets the file can read every session, note, product and spot in it.
If you save it in a cloud-synced folder (Google Drive, Dropbox and the like), it will be uploaded. Keep it somewhere private, and delete it when you\'re done.
Saved, unencrypted. Keep it private and delete it when you\'re done.
The export couldn\'t be saved. Try another place.
The file was created but didn\'t keep the export. Try saving it to your phone\'s storage, then copy it where you want it.
That file isn\'t an export of this journal.
This key is the only way back into your journal if you lose or reset this phone. There\'s no reset link and no backdoor, and nobody, not even us, can recover your journal without it.
Write it down and keep the paper somewhere safe, or keep it in a password manager. Not next to wherever you sync your journal: a key kept with the data it locks is no protection.
Your password manager, and its sync, become part of what protects your journal. Terpoir clears the clipboard after a minute.
We will never ask for your recovery key.
Without your recovery key, losing, resetting or replacing this phone means losing your journal for good. This key won\'t be shown again.
Type your recovery key from your saved copy. Capitals and dashes don\'t matter.
That\'s not the whole key yet: it has 56 characters.
There\'s a character that never appears in a recovery key.
That doesn\'t match. Check your copy for a typo.
That\'s a recovery key, but not this journal\'s.
Every protection on and every optional feature off. This is the default.

Turns on the conveniences that lean on your phone\'s platform: Google text recognition (on Google Play builds), opening lab-results links, the nearby-spot banner, spot names and details in alerts, follow-up check-ins, and the online map (where your version has one). Screen protection stays on, and \"Notify me\" stays your own choice. Some lines hold in every mode: no phone backups of your journal, no cloud model reading it, no analytics, and no Terpoir server.
What are you protecting this journal from? (Optional, and never saved.)
People who might pick up my phone
Not much, I just want it to work well
Then \"Most private\" fits, and it\'s already set. Relax anything below one switch at a time if you like.
YOLO Mode might suit you. Nothing changes until you review it.
This is your Privacy Center. Everything starts at its most private, and nothing changes unless you change it, here, whenever you like.
Nothing here yet. Tap New entry after your next session.
What were you hoping this would help with? For each one, did it help?
How it\'s hitting: touch and hold, then flick up or down
The longer you hold, the harder it\'s hitting now. Then let go with a flick: up if it\'s still climbing, down if it\'s easing off, or just let go if it\'s steady.
Drag a point up or down, or tap a guess to keep it. Dashed points are a guess until you set them.
What you entered here won\'t be saved.
It was saved when you added a note. Discarding deletes it, notes included, and its key is destroyed.
Its key is destroyed, so it can\'t be recovered, even from old backups or synced copies. Products stay.
Plain averages of your own ratings. One shows only when at least 5 rated sessions on each side differ by a star or more. Patterns, not advice.
No insights yet. Keep rating sessions; they appear once there is enough to compare.
%1$s averaged %2$s★, vs %3$s★ for your other sessions.

Sessions grouped by the Re-up Spot each product came from: the shop picked on the session (From), the receipt it names, or the product\'s only shop in Where I buy it. A shop shows once it has 5 rated sessions.
From the timeline points you set, never the chart\'s guesses: the middle value over your sessions. Shows once 3 sessions have points.

Products with %1$s as the top terpene
Choose what to share. Private details start switched off.
Once shared, this is outside Terpoir\'s protection.
Copied text is marked sensitive and cleared from the clipboard after a minute.
Check the amounts: numbers only, up to three decimals.
Check the timeline: whole minutes only.
Check the amounts: numbers only, up to three decimals.
Its key is destroyed, so it can\'t be recovered. Entries that used it stay, without its name.
Pick the ones that stand out. Most strains are known for one to three.
That\'s more than most strains are known for. Keep them if they all stand out; levels below can say which lead.
Rough levels, not percentages: those belong on products, from their labels. Leave any unrated.
Add a parent from your journal
Cannabinoids besides THC and CBD. Amounts belong on products.
How much a strain records. A lower step hides the extra fields; it never deletes what\'s saved.
Also the terpenes it\'s known for.
Also how much of each terpene, parent strains, and cannabinoids like CBN or CBG.
Indica and sativa labels are a rough guide; Terpoir\'s insights look at terpenes and cannabinoids instead.
Its key is destroyed, so it can\'t be recovered. Products that listed it stay.
Its key is destroyed, so it can\'t be recovered. Its products stay.
Fill the frame with the label and hold steady. The photo is read on your phone and then discarded.
Filled in from the label. Check each field before saving.
Point at a barcode, QR code or package tag. It is read on your phone; nothing is photographed.
Scan the label or package code
Fit the whole receipt in the frame. It is read on your phone and never saved: you check it on screen, and it is gone when you leave. Only the lines you confirm are saved.
\"Notify me\" alerts when you stop at a saved spot.
Reminders to note how a session went.
Tap to note how it\'s going.
The reminder needs permission to show notifications.
How\'s it going? Update what you feel now.
Precise location, so an alert means the right spot.
Location \"all the time\", so alerts work while Terpoir is closed. Android opens its settings for this: choose \"Allow all the time\".
Reading text needs Terpoir\'s open text recognition engine, a one-time download of a few megabytes from Google Play. It runs entirely on this phone: nothing you scan is sent anywhere.
The download didn\'t finish. Check that Google Play is available, then try again, or close this and enter the details by hand.
Text recognition couldn\'t start. Any codes were still read; enter the rest by hand.
Scanning needs the camera. Terpoir uses it only while this screen is open and never saves photos to your gallery.

Scanning uses the camera, only while this screen is open. Terpoir reads the picture on your phone and keeps it in memory: it isn\'t saved to your gallery or sent anywhere. Android will ask you to allow the camera next.
There are no other products to merge with.
\"%1$s\" is kept. What it lacks is filled in from \"%2$s\", whose sessions and purchases move to it, and then \"%2$s\" is deleted.
Changes not saved here yet are discarded.
Two of your products learned this exact line.
A receipt line printed exactly like one of these links to this product on its own.
That code belongs to %1$s. Open it instead?
A product with the same code is already in your journal. Record this batch on it instead of adding a duplicate?
A product with this name is already in your journal. Record this batch on it instead of adding a duplicate?
No app can open this link.
Opening lab-results links is off. You can turn it on in the Privacy Center.
Receipt photo with a box on each line that was read. The lines are also listed below it.
Tap the shop\'s name on the photo, or pick it from the lines below.
Part of the receipt is cut off. Retake?
Add the rest of the receipt
Photograph the rest of the receipt. Keep a few lines from the first photo at the top, so the two can be joined. It is read on your phone and never saved.
Couldn\'t find where the photos overlap. Take the second photo so it shows a few lines from the first.
Tap a line on the photo to add it. The photo is never saved.
Show the lines as a list
The amount needs a number above zero with up to three decimals, and the pack a whole number.
Matched to %1$s, as on an earlier receipt. Tap to undo.
No items were found. Add them with \"Missing a line?\" or \"Type a line\" below.
Its key is destroyed, so it can\'t be recovered.
Suggested from your words: check before adding
Pick any name. Terpoir never looks up an address, so the name is yours alone.
No location saved. A spot works fine as just a name.
Move the map until the circle is on the spot. Zoom in for a more exact point: the circle\'s size is how exact it is.
Couldn\'t get a location. Check that location is on, or save the spot without one.
Location permission wasn\'t granted. The spot can be saved without a location.
Coordinates are stored only inside your encrypted journal. Approximate is enough to recognize the neighborhood; precise pins the place.
Its key is destroyed, so it can\'t be recovered. Sessions at this spot stay, without it.
Showing nearby spots needs location while Terpoir is open.
Remind me to log purchases here
When you leave after a stop of a few minutes, Terpoir asks \"Quick log?\" once a day at most. The reminder never names this spot.
\"Quick log?\" after leaving a Re-up Spot you chose. Never names the place.

Speaking a note uses the microphone. Your phone\'s own speech recognizer turns it into text on the phone; the recording isn\'t kept or sent anywhere. Android will ask you to allow the microphone next.
Speech is turned into text on your phone. Nothing is sent anywhere, and the recording isn\'t kept.
People nearby can hear you. Switch to typing whenever you\'d rather not speak.
This phone has no on-device speech recognition, and Terpoir never uses online recognition. Type your note instead. A recognizer built into Terpoir is planned.
Your phone\'s on-device recognizer doesn\'t have this language installed. Add it in your phone\'s speech settings, or type instead.
Didn\'t catch that. Tap Speak to try again.
Speaking a note needs the microphone. Terpoir uses it only while you\'re speaking a note.
Speech recognition stopped. Try again, or type instead.
Voice notes are turned into text on your phone and never sent anywhere. The recording isn\'t kept.
Typed notes pass through your keyboard app, which sees everything you type.
Only if it isn\'t taken like other products of this type. The method sets its doses, timeline and check-in.
As soon as I leave Terpoir
Turning off the screen or locking your phone always locks Terpoir at once. Leaving the app always hides your journal from the app switcher.

With this setting, Terpoir behaves like your other apps: while your phone is unlocked, anyone you hand it to can open your journal if you used it recently, and its key stays in memory while the app is in the background. If you share your phone, choose \"As soon as I leave Terpoir\" or a short timer.
This shortcut was turned off in Terpoir.
One button that opens a new note. Shows nothing from your journal.
\"New note\" when you long-press the app icon
It shows only \"New note\", never anything from your journal. While your journal is locked, it opens a note you can write without unlocking: the note is sealed until you unlock.
Adds a \"New note\" tile you can place in Quick Settings: one swipe from anywhere to a new note, written without unlocking your journal and sealed until you unlock.
Nothing from your journal. The tile shows only \"New note\" and a neutral icon.

Anyone who pulls down your Quick Settings can see that the tile is there, as they could see the app icon. Anyone holding your unlocked phone could use it to add a note, but not to read anything; such notes are marked for you to keep or discard.
Turn it off here. The tile is removed from Quick Settings.
Adds a \"New note\" widget you can place on your home screen: one button and nothing else. Notes written from it don\'t need your journal unlocked and stay sealed until you unlock.
Nothing from your journal: no last session, ratings or names, only \"New note\".

Anyone who sees your home screen sees the button, as they could see the app icon. Anyone holding your unlocked phone could use it to add a note, but not to read anything; such notes are marked for you to keep or discard.
Turn it off here. The widget stops working and leaves the widget list; remove one already placed by long-pressing it.

Your journal stays locked. The note is sealed the moment you save it, and nobody can read it on this phone, you included, until you unlock. Then it appears in your journal to keep or discard, and you can add tags.
The note couldn\'t be saved. Try again, or unlock your journal.
Note saved and sealed. It joins your journal when you unlock.

resources.string: Only the chosen provider is ever contacted, and only while the online map is on. OpenFreeMap is free and run by one person on donations, so it could stop working one day.

With your own MapTiler key, the map comes from MapTiler instead. Get a key from your MapTiler account and paste it here. It\'s kept encrypted with your journal on this phone only, and never synced or exported.
MapTiler sees your IP address, the areas you look at and your key, which identifies your MapTiler account. Your use counts against your MapTiler plan.
A MapTiler key is saved on this phone.
A MapTiler key has only letters and digits.
Choose which details your journal keeps. Applies on every device you sync with.
Turn off what you don\'t care about, and Terpoir stops asking for it. Your choices apply on every device you sync with.
When, product, method, effects and rating are always tracked: they\'re what makes the journal and its insights work.
Who made a product. Products show without a brand when this is off.
Strains and their types (indica, sativa, hybrid).
What you paid and where. Receipts then record only what you bought and when.
Receipts and purchase history. Turning this off also turns off prices and shops.
Terpene amounts from the label, and the terpene insights built on them.
Batch or lot numbers and package dates, and freshness built on them.
How strong it felt over time.
How you felt before and after.
Keep it hidden: anything you saved stays, out of sight, and comes back if you turn %1$s on again. Delete: removes %1$s from every entry, on every device you sync with. Deleting can\'t be undone.
Shows Google\'s map when you pick a spot\'s location, instead of OpenFreeMap. The online map is turned on with it.

While you use the map, your IP address and the areas you look at go to Google, through Google Play services on your phone. Looking around a spot shows roughly where it is. Nothing from your journal is sent.

Google sees the areas you view. Play services is tied to your phone and Google account more closely than the other map providers are. Its maps connect to Google directly, not through Terpoir\'s network gate.
Turn the online map off, or choose another provider, in the Privacy Center. Terpoir then shows no Google map, but it can\'t clear what Play services cached for itself.

You can pick a spot\'s location on a map instead of using your phone\'s location. The map is optional and off unless you choose it here or later in the Privacy Center, where OpenFreeMap is also available.
